headline: Rainy and breezy today, mild midweek, with two wet, windy systems Friday through Sunday.
summary: A moist Pacific flow is bringing a front and a rainy, breezy day to western Washington. The front stalls offshore midweek, keeping things mild, with rain mostly along the coast and Olympics. Later in the week it moves inland, and forecasters now expect two separate wet, windy systems, one Friday and another Saturday night into Sunday. A dip in the jet stream, called an upper-level trough, then brings cooler air Sunday night and Monday, with snow levels falling toward the passes. The main worry is flooding in the Olympics and Mason County, where the Skokomish River may reach flood stage. Forecasters are fairly confident in the broad pattern but less sure of the weekend storm tracks, so where the strongest winds and rain land could shift.
